In the run-up to September 1939, political and economic chaos in the aftermath of World War I allowed Hitler in Germany, Mussolini in Italy and ultranationalists in imperial Japan to seize absolute power.

Germany took just four weeks to conquer Poland, using a new form of warfare, Blitzkrieg. Six armoured tank units known as Panzer divisions, supported by the Luftwaffe, quickly broke through Polish defences.

After the retreat from Dunkirk, Churchill rallied Britain in its darkest hour. Hitler was only just across the channel, but he reckoned without our supreme strategist, the might of the navy and the manoeuvrability of the air force.
Explores Hitler's assault on the Soviet Union in the summer of 1941.
The attack on Pearl Harbour brought the country nicknamed the 'sleeping giant', aka America, into the war, and saw the emergence of the aircraft carrier as the pre-eminent weapon of the seas.

Italian dictator Benito Mussolini dreamed of recreating the Roman Empire and making the Mediterranean the centre of a new vast colonial empire, including British-controlled Egypt and Sudan to the south.

With their armies fully engaged on the battlegrounds, the Allied and Axis powers focused their efforts to develop new weapons and new strategies to deliver a knockout blow to the enemy and bring about a quick end to the conflict.
After Hitler's gamble in the East fails, the Soviet Union starts to slowly push back and grow.

By early 1944, Hitler had long been expecting an Allied attack on north-western France, but his problem was knowing when and where it would come. This episode has a look at the Allied operations Bodyguard and Overlord.
Concentrates on Hitler's attempts to shift the balance of power back in his favour.
The war in the Pacific against Japan was a savage hand-to-hand, island-to-island struggle, fought by new specialist fighting units like the valiant Chindits.
Allied forces converge on Germany, uncovering the horrors of Belsen and Buchenwald, before pushing towards Berlin, where Adolf Hitler is clinging to power in his last desperate days.
A look at the conflict that brought the world to the brink of nuclear Armageddon.
The US Navy trained nearly 15,000 pilots on Lake Michigan from 1942-1945, resulting in the sinking of more than 100 classic World War II fighters and dive bombers.
The true story of two pilots, one American and the other Japanese, who confronted each other during a key WWII battle and, for some mysterious reason, did not shoot each other down.
Examining the Doolittle Raid on Tokyo from the perspectives of the children of the Doolittle Raiders and Chinese villagers who aided in their rescue.

In the darkest days of World War II in the Pacific, an elite British military team sought to facilitate espionage and sabotage behind enemy lines. This now famous group, the British Special Operations Executive or MI6, faced a critical obstacle.

Explore the complexities of the man who would become one of history's most infamous figures. From his obscure beginnings in Austria to his meteoric rise as Germany's Führer, dive deep into the forces that shaped Hitler's ideology and his leadership.

This documentary programme uses archival footage, interviews and dramatic reconstructions to tell the story of the rise of the Nazis through time as well as the continued rise of Neo-Nazis. `The Rise of the Nazi Party' reveals how the National Socialists exploited economic turmoil to get into power in Germany in 1933 before leading the nation into an era of genocide and military defeat. It profiles the people who helped the Nazis bring destruction to Europe, including Hitler, Himmler and Goebbels.
As punishment for the 1923 'Putsch', Hitler is banned from public speaking. Now he employs Joseph Goebbels to feed Hitler's political ideology to the masses.
Hitler seizes his chance in the wake of The Great Depression, turning the people on the incumbent Democratic Weimar Government and promising a brighter future.
A month after coming to power, Hitler addresses his people through the radio. He promises to make the economy his priority - and the task ahead is massive.
Hitler summons Germany's military leaders to a shock meeting at his headquarters. He lays out his plans for military expansion into neighbouring territories.
Alice Roberts explores the story of Stewart Britain by visiting Stirling, the home of the Scottish royals who eventually took the English throne in 1603 and created Great Britain.
Alice is in Lincoln, getting to grips with life in medieval England. She visits the magnificent cathedral that was once the tallest building in the world and re-lives the battle at Lincoln Castle.

Alice is in London, as she attempts to make sense of the world-changing events during the short but eventful Restoration period. She learns the violent and vengeful truth behind Charles II's carefully crafted public image.
In Portsmouth, Alice Roberts learns about Nelson's dark side, the heat of the battle at Trafalgar, the role of the Navy in the British Empire, and the lives of sex workers.
Alice Roberts visits Elizabethan Plymouth, exploring the story of England's 'Golden Age', from Sir Francis Drake to the Spanish Armada, piracy, theft, and the slave trade.
Alice Roberts explores Glasgow's age of steam, from lethal diseases and industrial injury to genteel tearooms, football at Celtic Park, and the beautiful Loch Katrine.
Over 3000 years ago, the Egyptian queen Teje became the source of inspiration for a religious revolution that created chaos in Egypt and may have paved the way for the world's largest religions.
The reign of Cleopatra II was even more turbulent than that of her famous, later namesake, Cleopatra VII, and this great queen saved her dynasty from being destroyed by hatred and strife.
The story of Cleopatra Selene, the little-known daughter of Cleopatra and Mark Antony, who witnessed her dynasty collapse amidst her parents' defeat and suicide but survived to become a great queen.
On the death of his regent, Hatshepsut, Thutmose III became pharaoh, and he immediately wanted to prove his worth during the Battle of Megiddo that pitted him against the kings of Canaan.
A battle worthy of Hollywood that established the glory of Ramses II when he faced the king Muwatalli II at Qadesh.
When Pharaoh Ptolemy IV confronts Antiochus the Great at Raphia, 100,000 men from the Mediterranean clash in a battle that uses military and naval strategies inspired by Alexander the Great.

Cleopatra attempts to restore the power of the early pharaohs through alliances with the most powerful men in the world. Her clash with Octavian at the battle of Actium leads to the rise of an emperor.

Bradley Walsh begins his journey with the pyramids. As a former Rolls-Royce engineer, Bradley questions theories about their construction. Armed with measuring tools and alternative hypothesis, he examines the Great Pyramid's exterior.

Bradley explores the Great Sphinx and the underground Serapeum with its precision-cut granite sarcophagi, questioning their purpose and links to the pyramid enigma. Travelling south, he visits the intricately designed Dendera Temple.
Bradley travels to the tomb of Tutankhamun to unravel the mysteries of the rise and fall of Egypt's most famous royal dynasty.
Professor Henning Franzmeier and his team of archaeologists undertake excavations in Pi-Ramses, hoping to discover the truth about the ancient Egyptian pharaoh Ramses II's lost city.
Henning Franzmeier and his team of archaeologists continue their search for the truth about Ramses the Great's lost city, uncovering new secrets and fascinating finds.

Im Norden von New Mexico führen Taylor Johnson und Jacob Cohen einen verzweifelten Kampf gegen Mutter Natur. Das 80 Jahre alte Lehmziegelhaus des Siedlerpaars wird von urwüchsigen Götterbäumen umwuchert. Auch die weitverzweigten Wurzeln sind ein Problem. Zudem hat der Vorbesitzer jede Menge Müll auf dem Grundstück vergraben, was ein Gesundheitsrisiko darstellt. Erst kürzlich hat ein Stromausfall die kostbaren Fleischvorräte vernichtet.

Bei einem Einsatz in Afghanistan wurde Travis Mills schwer verletzt. Doch der vierfach amputierte Ex-Soldat lässt sich nicht stoppen. Er hat eine Stiftung gegründet, die Veteranen hilft. Chase Morrill und sein Team wollen das Projekt unterstützen.

Familie Garcia hat sich für ein Leben in den Rocky Mountains entschieden. Doch ihr Aussteigerprojekt läuft nicht so wie geplant. Die Stromversorgung, mangelnde Nahrung und die Raubtiere bereiten Don und Lorinda große Sorgen.

Ryan McPherson betreibt eine Austernfarm in Maine. Dort zeigt er den Kunden, wie man die Muscheln züchtet und erntet. Chase Morill und sein Team verwandeln eine alte Bretterbude in ein schickes Gästehaus, in dem die Gäste unterkommen können.

Der Mietvertrag seiner Wohnung läuft bald aus und Nils ist bereit, sich sein erstes eigenes Zuhause zu kaufen. Da er sowieso die meiste Zeit bei der Arbeit oder beim Feiern verbringt, sucht er nach einem winzigen Unterschlupf, der pflegeleicht ist.

Für Jessica ist ein wichtiger Teil des Erwachsenwerdens, ein Haus zu kaufen. Da sie aber noch einen Studentenkredit abzahlen muss, hat sie sich für ein winziges Haus entschieden. Sie freut sich darauf, das perfekte Zuhause für sich zu finden.

Bethany und Matthew wollen ihr Leben vereinfachen und planen, mit dem Ziel finanzielle Freiheit zu erreichen, ihr über 200 Quadratmeter großes Zuhause zu verkaufen. Sie haben ihre fünfköpfige Familie bei Bethanys Eltern einquartiert, während sie sich nach einem winzigen Haus umsehen. Sie suchen ein Häuschen, das ihre wachsende Familie aufnehmen kann, ohne ihr Budget zu sprengen. Für ihre Suche sind sie über 3.000 Kilometer nach Nampa, Idaho, gefahren, um etwas Passendes zu finden.

Joy und LaToya wollen nach Escondido, Kalifornien, ziehen. Um ein schuldenfreies Leben führen zu können, wünschen sie sich ein Minihaus. Da beide von zu Hause aus arbeiten, benötigen sie viel Platz und wollen dabei auch auf Luxus nicht verzichten.

Mel und Carson aus Nebraska möchten gern reisen und suchen deshalb nach einem kleinen mobilen Haus. Sie wollen darin leben und arbeiten, wenn sie von US-Bundesstaat zu Bundesstaat reisen. Carson wünscht sich eine Bleibe mit weniger als 18 Quadratmetern, doch Mel fällt es schwer, sich von ihrem mehr als 80 Quadratmeter großen Apartment zu trennen. Mel ist bereit, sich zu verkleinern, aber hofft auf einige Annehmlichkeiten wie in einem großen Haus.

Tommo und Megsy, die lange auf einem Kreuzfahrtschiff gearbeitet haben, wollen in Mérida in Mexiko sesshaft werden und ihre Reiseerfahrungen in einem Blog teilen. Doch zuerst müssen sie sich auf den mexikanischen Wohnungsmarkt begeben.

Amy und Clyde aus Highlands Ranch in Colorado wollen mit ihren Kindern nach Playa Tambor in Costa Rica auswandern. Dort suchen sie ein möbliertes Haus mit vier Schlafzimmern, nur über die Lage können sie sich nicht einigen.

Puvin und Chirvani träumen davon, Paris kennenzulernen, bevor sie eine Familie gründen. Doch obwohl Puvin bereits einen Job dort hat, ist das Wohnungsbudget der beiden sehr begrenzt - und die Mieten in Paris sind extrem hoch.

Paul aus Tucson, Arizona, bekommt das Angebot, an der Universität von Bern seine Doktorarbeit zu schreiben. So erfüllt er den Traum seiner Freundin Hilary. Diese hat jedoch keinen Job und daher ist das Budget der beiden begrenzt.

Stella und Esther sind beide von den Niederlanden nach Barcelona gezogen. Zufälligerweise haben beide Frauen am selben Tag in derselben Firma einen neuen Job angefangen. So sind sie besonders schnell beste Freundinnen geworden.

Zwei texanische Unternehmer suchen ein Haus, das ihren beruflichen Erfolg widerspiegelt. Gleichzeitig träumt ein Paar aus der Filmbranche von einem Neuanfang. Die Brüder begleiten beide Parteien bei der Suche nach einem Zuhause im Wilden Westen.

Zwei Großstädter wollen ihr Leben neu ausrichten und suchen fernab von Bildschirmen und Großstadtstress nach einem Ort für ihre Hochzeitslocation. Jonathan und Drew begleiten sie in eine ehemalige kalifornische Minenstadt, wo nicht nur das passende Anwesen gefunden werden soll, sondern auch ein neues Lebensgefühl. Zusätzlich helfen die Brüder einem kanadischen Pferdetrainer, in Arizona Fuß zu fassen.

Auf der Ranch bedeutet Sommer immer Arbeit und Freude zugleich. Während Austin mit den Söhnen die Zäune streicht, packt Elizabeth einen Picknickkorb mit Blaubeerkuchen, Caprese-Sandwiches und Holunderschorle.

Zur Lavendelernte versammelt Elizabeth Freunde und Familie auf der Ranch. Sie serviert als Dank Hähnchen Piri Piri und einen Zitronenkuchen mit feiner Buttercreme. So wird die Erntezeit zu einem Moment des gemeinsamen Genießens.

Auf der Ranch bedankt sich Elizabeth bei ihren Nachbarn, die ihr im Alltag zur Seite stehen. Sie kocht eine herzhafte Mais-Lasagne und backt duftende Kirsch-Mandel-Scones. Es ist ein einfaches Essen, mit dem sie ihre Wertschätzung zeigt.

Wenn Elizabeths Cousins zu Besuch kommen, wird die Ranch immer zum Treffpunkt für Familie und Erinnerungen. Nach einem Tag voller gemeinsamer Arbeit kocht sie Hähnchen Marsala und reicht warmen Schokoladenkuchen als Dessert.

Becca und Damian sind in ein Haus aus dem 19. Jahrhundert im malerischen Cornwall gezogen. Im Erdgeschoss befindet sich eine noch unbrauchbare Küche, deswegen entwerfen Paul und Helen eine Küche, die den Lebensstil der Familie unterstreicht.

Frieda und Javvy leben mit ihren beiden Kindern in einem Schloss an der Küste in Cornwall. Sie wünschen sich eine Küche, die einem König würdig ist. Paul und Helen nehmen die Herausforderung an und entwerfen eine Küche für zwei Kreativschaffende.

In dem malerischen Ocean Shores sucht ein Ehepaar mit seiner Tochter ein Ferienhaus. Dort wollen sie eine schöne Zeit mit ihrer ganzen Familie verbringen können, während sie sich ein Haus direkt am Wasser mit drei Schlafzimmern wünschen.

Ein Ehepaar sucht nach einem bezahlbaren Ferienhaus auf Whidbey Island, eine recht teure Gegend, für sich und ihre drei Söhne. Nachdem sie ein tolles Haus gefunden haben, muss die fünfköpfige Familie nun die Renovierungsarbeiten selbst übernehmen.

Daphne und Ian arbeiten mit Hochdruck daran, das Torhaus ihres Schlosses endlich fertigzustellen. Neben einer Galerie mit Blick auf das Schloss entstehen ein auffälliger Kronleuchter und ein maßgefertigter Katzenbaum für Kater Charlie.

Dick und Angel helfen einer Frau, ihr Sommerhaus in einen farbenfrohen tropischen Rückzugsort zu verwandeln. An anderer Stelle hilft Dick zwei Erzieherinnen beim Bau eines Vogelverstecks, während Angel ein eigenes Projekt hat.

Nach sechs Jahren kehren Will und Lauren wieder zurück in ihre Heimatstadt Waco, Texas. Sie möchten, dass ihre beiden Töchter in einem Traumhaus aufwachsen. Dieses hoffen sie mit einem Budget von 300.000 Dollar zu finden.

Ein Pärchen zieht mit seinem Sohn von Denver nach Waco um. Es hofft, dort ein entspannteres Leben führen zu können, und zwar in einem stylischen Haus im Grünen. Mit einem Budget von 450.000 Dollar sucht das Paar nach seinem Traumhaus.

Der Veranstaltungsraum von Wetumpka wurde nach der ersten weiblichen Bürgermeisterin benannt. Ben und Erin wollen dieses Stück Geschichte wieder aufleben lassen, indem sie den Raum modernisieren und für Hochzeiten, Tagungen und Partys aufbereiten.

Ben und Erin wollen mit Farbe und Pinsel das Straßenbild und zugleich die Stimmung der Stadt ändern. Damit wollen sie der kreativen Kulturszene von Wetumpka Tribut zollen. Außerdem überraschen sie ein Paar mit einer Renovierung ihres Hauses.

Ben und Erin sind mit einem geschichtsträchtigen Altbau beschäftigt, um einen Neubau zu erschaffen. Chip und Stephanie hingegen leben zusammen in einem Haus, das im Jahr 1850 erbaut wurde und später mit zwei weiteren Häusern verbunden wurde.

A three-bedroom semi in Crewe, a top-floor flat in London and a terraced house in Oldham are sold under the hammer. All the owners are happy with the prices they paid, but will any of them be able to turn a profit at the end of the projects?

While developers in Croydon in Surrey and Donnington in Shropshire wrestle with whether to lose a bedroom each for a better placed kitchen or bathroom, two friends in Derby consider creating two more in their six-bedroom house.

Two brothers buy a rundown cottage in Probus in Cornwall, a father buys a flat in Mitcham in Surrey as a long-term investment for his young daughter and a seasoned property developer buys a house in Tunstall in Stoke-on-Trent for her daughter.

Martin Roberts, Lucy Alexander and Dion Dublin are in Stoke, Croydon in London and Warrington hearing tales from the auction rooms.

Three developers have very different reasons for making their investments: there's a family home in Consett in County Durham, a rental investment in Derby and an auction buy in Beckenham in London which will be used to run a new business, which the owner hopes will give him more time with his family.

A flat with huge potential in London's Earlsfield, and terraced houses in Wombourne near Wolverhampton and Ynyswen near Treorchy in Wales are all sold under the hammer.

Martin is impressed with the potential of two shops and three flats in Tonypandy in Wales while Dion looks round a two-bedroom maisonette in Dawley and Lucy meets a first-time developer with ambitious plans for an end terrace in London's Forest Gate.
A first-floor one-bedroom flat in London's Stepney Green, a three-bed semi in Dartford in Kent and a one-bedroom flat on the 17th floor of a block in Salford are all sold under the hammer.

A 1930s bungalow in Dereham in Norfolk, a first-floor flat in London's East Ham and a property in Maryport in Cumbria with a hidden room are all sold at auction. Martin, Lucy and Dion meet the new owners and hear their plans for their investments.

For two of the properties sold under the hammer, a semi in Ilkeston in Derby and a flat in Streatham Hill in London, it's all about creating smart kitchens and bathrooms. Meanwhile, the owners of a bungalow have to deal with an unexpected issue.

A fifth-floor flat in Greater Manchester, a three-bed semi in Carlisle and three commercial buildings near Stansted are all sold under the hammer. One developer has a pressing deadline to finish his renovation work.

An old Derbyshire farmhouse in Wirksworth gets a stunning makeover, a developer builds a pair of semis in Chatham in Kent, while a mid-terraced house in Blackhall Colliery in County Durham is given a makeover ready for the rental market.

Martin, Lucy and Dion meet father-and-daughter developers. An apartment in a former mill in Mow Cop on the Staffordshire and Cheshire border, a three-bed semi in East Ham and a flat in Bournemouth are all given makeovers with the help of dad.

A couple about to get married buy their first home in Newcastle, a new dad thinks developing a flat in Leyton in London will give him more time with his four-month-old son, and a former IT worker develops a property in Gainsborough in Lincolnshire.
A flat over two floors in London's Camberwell, another flat in Telford in Shropshire and a three-bed semi in Alvaston in Derby are all sold under the hammer.
Martin, Lucy and Dion visit a grand five-bedroom period house in Folkestone in Kent, a two-bedroom flat in London's Leytonstone and a two-bedroom mid-terrace in Fenton in Stoke-on-Trent.

Heather and John love Greece so much that they want their very own characterful bolthole on Crete. They've fallen in love with northern Crete, and it's easy to see why. With its stunning historic towns, it's perfect for a relaxing lifestyle.

Entertainment manager James hopes to blow his guests away with a menu inspired by his travels to Nashville, Tennessee. His Americana-themed finger food menu and extravagant exercise class keep his guests on their toes.

The penultimate host in and around Manchester is jeweller Angela, who's hoping to bedazzle her guests with a traditional all-Italian, tried-and-tested menu that's been passed down the generations for many years.

The second visit is to Rigsby's Guest House in Doncaster, South Yorkshire, run by Tracy Ward. The lack of en-suite bathrooms causes a stink, and some guests cannot figure out the pricing.

Thierry Paulin machte drei Jahre Raubzüge durch die Gegend um Montmartre, um an Geld und Wertsachen zu kommen und sich seine Drogensucht und den extravaganten Lebensstil zu finanzieren. Noch vor seinem Prozess starb er 1989 im Gefängnis an AIDS.

Der Ku-Klux-Klan ist die älteste Terrorgruppe der USA. Ein Geheimbund weißer Rassisten, die Hass auf Schwarze predigen. Die Verbrechen seiner Mitglieder erschüttern die Nation seit mehr als 150 Jahren. Teil 1 der Dokumentation beschreibt die Anfänge des Klans in der Zeit nach dem amerikanischen Bürgerkrieg, sein Wiedererstarken nach dem Kino-Blockbuster Die Geburt einer Nation, seinen wachsenden Einfluss auf das politische Leben in den USA und seinen erneuten Niedergang im Zweiten Weltkrieg.

Der Ku-Klux-Klan ist die älteste terroristische Organisation der USA. In Reaktion auf die Bürgerrechtsbewegung der 1960er Jahre erlebt auch der Ku-Klux-Klan einen neuen Aufschwung - vornehmlich in den Südstaaten.

Eine große Mission steht der Antonow An-225 bevor: In nur vier Wochen sollen schwere Transformatoren von Chile aus über die Anden nach Bolivien geflogen werden. Das ist eine logistische Herausforderung für das größte Frachtflugzeug der Welt.

Stoßzeit am Flughafen München: Ein Airbus A350 hebt ab. Das Langstrecken-Großraumflugzeug des europäischen Flugzeugherstellers soll seinem größten Konkurrenten, der US-amerikanischen Boeing 787 Dreamliner, den Kampf ansagen. Unter allen Verkehrsflugzeugen weist der A350 den höchsten Anteil an Kohlefaserstoffen in Rumpf und Tragflächen auf und setzt somit neue Stabilitätsmaßstäbe bei hohem Komfort. Zweieinhalb Monate dauert die Montage des Überfliegers. Kann Boeing da noch mithalten?

Nach diversen Vorfällen steigt in der deutschen Bevölkerung die Furcht, Opfer eines Übergriffs zu werden und damit auch die Nachfrage an Schutzmaßnahmen. Zahlreiche Bürger bereiten sich daher technisch und körperlich auf die Selbstverteidigung vor.

Aufgrund der häufigen Unfälle auf Deutschlands Straßen führt die Autobahnpolizei regelmäßige Kontrollen durch. So versucht sie, vor allem Lkw-Unfällen vorzubeugen. Doch nicht nur Prävention ist ihr Ressort, sondern auch die Kriminalitätsbekämpfung.
Es werden diesmal drei reale Katastrophen seziert: Atomrakete, Fähre und Ölplattform.

Katastrophen haben viele Gesichter. Doch sie alle beginnen mit einer Verkettung scheinbar kleiner Ursachen. Mit modernster 3D-Visualisierung, präziser Simulationstechnik und wissenschaftlicher Analyse werden reale Unglücke rekonstruiert.

Ein Angler aus der Ukraine und eine junge Frau aus Brasilien geraten ins Visier der Zollbeamten. An den Flughäfen Auckland und Queenstown machen Beamte Funde, die die Biosicherheit des Kontinents und Landes gefährden können.
Eine Kanadierin unternimmt den Versuch, eine Katze über die Grenze zu schmuggeln und ein Niederländer wird mit einer immensen Menge an Kokain aufgegriffen.

Ein Mexikaner kommt aufgrund der Textnachrichten auf seinem Handy in Schwierigkeiten. Außerdem finden Zollbeamte im Gepäck eines chinesischen Geschäftsmanns sowie bei einem Paar sonderbare Gegenstände, die eine genauere Untersuchung erfordern.

Zollbeamte in Christchurch finden bei einer Kontrolle eine Bibel, die mehr als nur Worte enthält. Außerdem entdecken sie einen Korb, in dem sich diverse Teile eines toten Schweins befinden. Zudem wird ein Tabakschmugglerring in Queenstown entdeckt.

Die Zollbeamten in Queenstown, das sich im Süden von Neuseeland befindet, werden auf einen französischen Arzt aufmerksam. Außerdem gerät ein Zwillingspaar aus Taiwan in Schwierigkeiten. Es wird auf jeden Fall mit spürbaren Sanktionen rechnen müssen.

Zollbeamte werden auf Personen aufmerksam, die Kokain konsumieren. Außerdem wird in der Poststelle ein dubioses Fläschchen gefunden, in dem sich angeblich Reinigungsmittel befinden soll. Eine Untersuchung wird eingeleitet.

Der Bugatti Chiron ist eine perfekte Symbiose aus den Attributen Schönheit und Biest. Er ist einer der schnellsten Sportwagen, büßt dadurch jedoch nichts von seiner Eleganz ein. Es werden nur hochwertige Materialien verwendet. 1.500 PS runden ihn ab.

Tesla hat gezeigt, dass für Höchstleistungen kein Verbrennungsmotor notwendig ist. Der Rimac C Two macht da keine Ausnahme. Das reine E-Auto erreicht eine Spitzengeschwindigkeit von 415 km/h. Ein modernes Fahrerassistenzsystem darf nicht fehlen.
Wer denkt, Frauen seien das schwächere Geschlecht, hat nicht mit Jeannine Jourdan gerechnet.
Speditionen und LKW-Fahrer werden bei ihrer herausfordernden Arbeit in ganz Europa gezeigt.

1953 gräbt ein Team von Archäologen in den Ruinen der antiken Stadt Jericho ein seltsames Objekt aus, das einem deformierten Kopf ähnelt. Es wird als Jericho Head bekannt. Es ist fast 10.000 Jahre alt und scheint aus Ton zu bestehen.

Im Jahr 1928 entdeckt ein Arbeiter bei Grabungen in der antiken babylonischen Stadt Ur die Überreste einer Holzkiste, die Archäologen seit fast einem Jahrhundert fasziniert. Es ist trapezförmig, 48 cm lang und 21 cm hoch.

Die Schweizer Alpen sind die imposante Kulisse für die Fahrt im Bernina Express. Auf seiner Fahrt von Chur im Kanton Graubünden über das Wintersportmekka St. Moritz bis ins italienische Tirano überwindet der Zugklassiker mehr als tausend Höhenmeter.

Der Pride of Africa rollt in der Süd-Nord-Tour durch das atemberaubende Südafrika. Wilde Tiere und spektakuläre Natur begleiten die Passagiere. Die Etappen der Reise sind geprägt durch ein Naturreservat, die Wüste oder das Land der tausend Hügel.

Diesmal geht es um ein Herrenhaus in Irland und um ein verlassenes Krankenhaus auf Hokkaido, in dem es spuken soll. In Georgien wird eine Festung aus der Römerzeit wiederentdeckt und vor der Küste Mosambiks verfällt ein ehemaliges Luxushotel.

Man blickt auf ein verlassenes brasilianisches Inselgefängnis, in dem einst ein Aufstand ausgebrochen war. Zudem birgt ein texanisches Luxushotel eine kriminelle Vergangenheit. Außerdem besuchen wir ein verlassenes koreanisches Internat.

Eine ehemalige Garnison für US-Soldaten macht inzwischen eher den Eindruck eines Feriendorfes. Außerdem wird Napoleons Mission in Russland und seine Schwierigkeiten dabei thematisiert. Zudem geht es um einen Staudamm in Wales.

Einst waren zwei riesige Satelliten in Georgia in den USA als Telefonanlagen errichtet worden. Diesen Nutzen hatten sie nicht lange inne. Als sie dafür nicht mehr gebraucht wurden, verwendete man sie für die Suche nach außerirdischem Leben.

Besucht wird die Ruine des ehemaligen Hartwood Hospital in Schottland, welches Angst einjagt. Fraglich ist, welche Experimente dort an den Patienten durchgeführt wurden. Gesucht wird auch nach den sagenumwobenen Hängenden Gärten von Babylon.

Gesucht wird nach einem Vier-Millionen-Vermögen in den philippinischen Gewässern nahe Corregidors. Untersucht wird auch das Missouri State Penitentiary in Jefferson City, in welchem viele berüchtigte Verbrecher inhaftiert sind.

Im April 1945 starten die Sowjets den wohl größten Artillerieangriff aller Zeiten. Über eine Million Rotarmisten, tausende Panzer und eine Armada schwerer Geschütze rücken auf die deutsche Hauptstadt Berlin vor, um zu kämpfen.

Für die Ardennenoffensive 1944 mobilisiert Hitler seine letzten Reserven und zieht dafür Truppen von der umkämpften Ostfront ab. Bei dieser Entscheidungsschlacht will er einen Keil zwischen die Nord- und die Südflanke der Westalliierten treiben.
The story of the Allied forces trying to free Europe by fighting Nazi fanatics until the last man is standing.
In July 1944, French resistance fighters called Maquisards declared a Free French Republic on the remote Vercors plateau in eastern France to support the Allied invasion of Normandy.
An Amazon cargo plane nosedives into a swamp outside Houston, the evidence eventually leads investigators to a pilot with a long history of failures.
EgyptAir Flight 804 suddenly spirals into the Mediterranean Sea. Although early evidence suggests a fire broke out on board, Egyptian authorities say it was an act of terror.
Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX 8, nosedives after takeoff from Addis Ababa, killing everyone on board.
Shortly after taking off, a fire breaks out on UPS Flight 6. As smoke fills the cockpit, getting the plane safely back is a race against time.
On a secret mission over Africa with the UN Secretary General on board, the United Nations DC-6 mysteriously crashes 10 miles from the runway.
Investigating Chalk's Ocean Airways flight 101, which crashed just after take-off from Watson Island in Miami on 19 December 2005, killing 20 people.
Thord and his young crew battle a blizzard to rescue a truck that blocks one lane of a major road.
Despite severe injuries, Captain Matt Urban returns to the front line to spearhead a daring Sherman tank assault during the Allied breakout in Normandy.
Legendary Canadian regiment suffers devastating losses.
Former slave labourers at the Sobibor death camp in German-occupied Poland discuss their lives as prisoners and share the story of their desperate and courageous escape on 14 October 1943.
In the final year of the Second World War, the infamous Panzer elite division Das Reich was known for its mass murders on the Eastern Front.
With 15,000 men and more than 200 tanks, Das Reich took six days to reach Normandy from the south of France, massacring civilians along the way.
Experts investigate the collision of two planes over the Grand Canyon in 1956, uncovering a frightening problem that threatened the entire aviation system.

En route to Hong Kong, Cathay Pacific Flight 780 is high over the South China Sea when both of the plane's engines fail, turning the Airbus A-330 into a 200-ton glider. The captain takes over manual control and manages to power up one engine.
After losing two engines near enemy territory, US Air Force pilots abort their refuelling mission and attempt to land their damaged plane.
Explaining and investigating the world's most infamous plane crashes.
Belief in demons is centuries old, but modern popular culture means they endure.

The team use cutting edge visual effects to 'drain' the waters around the notorious island of Alcatraz. With the waters drained away, the secrets of Alcatraz are revealed, including exactly why the island's infamous prison was so inescapable.
With capacity at an all-time high, have a look at the prisoners of the overflowing cell blocks of Casuarina maximum security prison, which houses Australia's most deadly criminals.
With the season almost upon them, the commercial salmon captains of Cook Inlet are ready for action. Each fisherman has something to prove.
As the final surge hits, Tom asks: Who survives, and at what cost? New evidence reveals the fate of three real Romans.
After a spearfisherman is mauled by a shark, researchers begin to wonder if animals in the wild can offer clues as to how to outsmart these perfect predators.
In the oppressive heat of the African dunes and deserts, only the strong survive. A look at the exceptional animals that use brains and brawn to thrive in this unforgiving environment.
The fearsome and powerful Nile crocodiles await the violent fights between hippos. The waterholes of Africa are the stage for one of the continent's greatest spectacles.
Dr Oakley visits with an angry cat that may have diabetes and a dog with a gland problem.
The Schroeders reel in an unexpected catch during a family boating trip.
The docs save a cat that can't pee and rescue a St. Bernard's dying tongue.
These small, furry animals may seem mild-mannered, but there are secret skills behind their survival in human environments.
Ho, oh, no. It's Christmas season in Michigan and Dr Pol and his team make their patient list, check it twice, and treat those who are naughty, spotty, snotty and nice.
It's a dog's world at Pol Clinic, and the vets have their paws full of a crew of pups.

Hannah Fry explores Vietnam's remarkable post-war transformation. From moped chaos in Ho Chi Minh City to the muddy graft of prawn harvest in the Mekong Delta and a restorative spa bath in Sapa, Hannah reveals a nation embracing change.

Hannah Fry journeys across islands, mountains and olive groves to reveal why ancient Greece was the birthplace of so many big ideas. She decodes the Parthenon's geometry, sails the Aegean with ancient tools, tries her hand at olive farming, and more.
Stanley explores the pioneering spirit of Italy's industrial heartland, where the cuisine and ingredients are defiantly forward-thinking.
Stanley delves into the identity of Italy's northernmost region, where many speak German as well as Italian, and the cuisine reflects both cultures.

Stanley discovers surprises in this wild region he has never visited before; he investigates how the rugged terrain influences the food and culture; high in sheep country, he prepares mutton on a traditional barbecue.
Meet some of the adorable youngsters that grow up in the iconic Australian bush.
The Critter Fixer team helps a few best friends who bite off more than they can chew. Olive the dog feasted on an entire tennis ball. (S5 Ep2)
As the wave hits Sri Lanka and the tragedy expands across the Indian Ocean, journalists strive to understand the scope of events so that they can convey it to the rest of the world.
Tourists on an island band together to survive in the aftermath of a tsunami. Though there are hundreds of casualties, they must work hard to save as many lives as possible.
Climate change means warmer ocean temperatures and higher sea levels which are intensifying hurricanes. Some experts say we should add a Category six to the Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind scale.
When on the hunt, snakes judge to perfection the very instant that separates life from death.
The host presents comprehensive coverage of political, social and economic topics, offering insights from specialists to clarify complex matters.
A mixed news bulletin which keeps viewers updated with the current affairs.
Featuring the latest in technology, innovations, gadgets, and digital trends, offering insights, expert reviews, and updates shaping the future of modern life.
A show that traces India's trajectory towards being a Superpower in Geo-politics and Economy.
The breakfast show that sets the agenda for the day.
FAULTLINES WITH GAURIE DWIVEDI - BEHIND FRACTURED BOUNDARIES... WE CLEAR THE FOG OF WAR.
Exploring the world of automobiles, from in-depth vehicle reviews and exclusive interviews to the latest trends in automotive culture, urban mobility, electric vehicles, and travel adventures.
In this show, we interact with the Asian community to see what makes the people tick & try and explore the challenges and issues they face.
Watch TV programmes and films instantly.
Greta Van Susteren gives the big news from D.C., N.Y., across America, and around the world.
Ed Henry offers his common-sense take on the news, helping viewers better understand the deeper details behind today's stories.

Sec. Marco Rubio visits Israel; IDSF Chairman Amir Avivi shares his insight; Fleur Hassan-Nahoum, Israel Special Envoy for Trade and Innovation, discusses Charlie Kirk's legacy and his support of Israel.
Hosted by former Navy SEAL Kaj Larsen, Tactical Wealth explores life after service, business, and building wealth.
Carl Higbie gives common-sense news analysis, exposes government and media bias, as he fights for American values.
Rob Schmitt wraps up all the latest news and opinion and sets the stage for tomorrow.
Raw bodycam footage capturing high-stake police incidents.
The legacies of history's most notorious cult leaders.
Looking at the numerous missteps that turned the Axis powers' devastating victories into crushing defeats.

A history of UFO's and Presidents, from George Washington to Donald Trump, with expert testimony, interviews, and reports of personal encounters involving U.S. Presidents and unexplained paranormal phenomena.

The Swiss Guard has protected the Pope and the Vatican for over 500 years. Explore the history, secret missions, traditions, and modern-day responsibilities of the world's most distinctive military corps.
Hitler's Wehrmacht invades the Soviet Union in 1941; the invasion had been planned under the name Barbarossa.

On September 1, 1939, Germany invades Poland starting the greatest war the world has ever known; six million Jews and countless "undesirables" were exterminated by the Nazis; there were millions of Allied and Axis casualties.
Norm Christie investigates the often unknown stories behind history's battles.
Imagery, rarely seen archival materials and interviews provide insight into the life and history of former Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin.
From the 9/11 attacks and Hurricane Katrina to the U.S. housing market and Obama's presidency, the 2000s brought a decade of chaos.
John Bachman focuses on the biggest news from D.C., N.Y., and around America.
Hard-hitting analysis and opinion on the latest news and events delivered.
Greg Kelly provides hard-hitting reports and analysis from Los Angeles to New York and the Beltway to the Rust Belt.
Rob Carson dissects politics, cultural phenomena and the absurdity confronting America with humor and satire.
It's the day of the duck race! When Miss Rabbit gives the sign, everyone drops their ducks in the river at the first bridge - whose will make it to the second bridge first?

At the gym, Madame Gazelle is teaching the children about martial arts. Along with Mr. Bull, the children learn how to fall safely, balance and even how to throw punches in the right stance. Mr. Bull gives them their white belts.

Dr Hamster has brought a giant ant farm and opens the ant farm's lid to show how they got in. Nobody noticed they escaped and starting moving things in the classroom! The children place food around to lead the ants safely back.
Grampy Rabbit gives Peppa and her friends a tour of an exercise park. Since the machines are only for grownups, the kids do funny exercises instead.
The elves give the King some chickens from the Elf Farm so that he can have eggs whenever he likes.
When the fairies wake up to find that their wands are not working, the kingdom has to cope without any help from magic for the entire day.

Mummy Pig is determined that George's new hat doesn't get muddy when Peppa and George visit Grandpa and Granny Pig. Everyone tries to make sure that it stays clean, even if it means that they get messy instead.
Mummy Dog surprises Captain Daddy Dog with a gift of a boat trip for his birthday, but when Peppa and the gang come along, the trip doesn't go to plan.
Peppa and George explore the greenhouse, and it is full of lovely tomatoes and basil. When it is time for dinner, Granny Pig takes all the ingredients they have grown and makes a tasty salad.
Peppa and George go sailing with Grandpa Pig, but when he keeps getting stuck in the mud, they all decide to have a sleepover on the boat while they wait for the tide to come back in.
Peppa is playing at Suzy's house, and they find out that Granny Sheep is moving in. She transforms the dull spare room and attic into an exotic boudoir and creative studio for her to make things.
On a rainy day, Granny Sheep plays in the garden with Peppa and Suzy. They decide to play with cardboard boxes and build a hospital, a cookie factory, and a train station.

Peppa and her friends are at the clubhouse. They are playing at serving takeaway food. The children assign themselves different roles, including a cook and a waiter. Once the imaginary food is ready, they have fun delivering it.
Peppa and George play with walkie-talkies at Granny and Grandpa Pig's house. Grandpa Pig teaches Peppa and George how to use codenames to talk using the gadgets.
Peppa is intrigued to see her parents go to work every day. Daddy Pig makes Peppa her very own office to make her feel good.
Peppa finds a small bird on the ground in the garden of her house. She takes him to Dr Hamster, who explains that it is a swift and is probably tired after a long journey.
When Thomas meets some buzz-worthy newcomers who need help finding a home, the tank engine and his friends come to the rescue.

It's Earth Day and Paddington has the important job of planting a tree. He has to find the perfect spot before it is too late. Baaz holds a spring harvest festival and everyone enjoys bringing their own celebration along.

Who is Paddington's Special Visitor that Jonathan and Judy have helped come from afar? It's the last night of Hanukkah and Mr Gruber's Hanukkiah breaks before he can light the final candle, how can another be found in time?
Paddington and his friends help PC Wells solve a mysterious case. Inspired by Aunt Lucy's special recipe, the Browns start a takeaway business from their home, but it proves to be hard work.
Paddington has to decide whether to support England or Peru before the football match, but he loves both countries. It's time for Aunt Lucy to go home, but there's still time for one last adventure.

Peppa and friends are at Penny Polar Bear's house for a movie night; before they can watch it, the children need to decide where to sit, which popcorn to eat and take a toilet break -- then they're finally ready.
Granny Sheep and Suzy take Granny Pig and Peppa around Art House Day; after a day full of screen printing and silhouette miniatures, Granny Pig finds an art piece at Suzy's house.
Madame Gazelle and Mr Bull lead the children to the wildflower wood to learn all about flowers; the children enjoy identifying the flowers like Wild Garlic, Bluebells and even a rare orchid.
Peppa and George play in their grandparents' garden on a very hot day, but they don't have a paddling pool; Granny and Grandpa Pig create their own water squeezers and even a water slide.
Mummy Elephant invites Peppa and Daddy Pig to perform magic at Emily's birthday party. Peppa shows her friends how the magic trick works.
Daddy Pig receives a jumping stick in the mail and demonstrates to Peppa and George how to use it. Peppa and her friends struggle with using it first.
Miss Rabbit gives Peppa and her friends a tennis lesson, but the tennis balls get everywhere. Mr Stallion and Miss Corgi arrive with strawberries and cream.
Peppa and her family are on a caravan adventure; the first stop is the biggest potato in the world; when it starts to get too foggy, they park up for a rest before another busy day.
During Pie Swap Day in Adventure Bay, Humdinger sends Rocky Kitty to take one of Mr Porter's delicious pies so he can join the contest.
When Ms. Marjorie brings her bookmobile to Everest and the kids of the mountains, Maynard accidentally sets the van rolling and goes off on a wild ride.

Paddington and the Browns rescue pufflings, who get lost around the campsite instead of taking their first flight. Paddington enjoys a diving adventure with Jonathan and Judy - but where is her necklace?

The beach is a mess, but all the litter must be cleared up in time for the beach party that everyone has been looking forward to. As the summer holidays come to an end, the time arrives to say goodbye to new friends.
Paddington builds a robot that he calls Paddington that requires a real friend to work, Baaz invites everyone to celebrate Diwali with him, and Paddington is his helpful assistant.
Tim goes to DinoStar's training academy but is confused by his hero's training methods.
The Rex family go on a long road trip through the galaxy to get to Rocket World.
Join Tim Rex, brother Tommy, sister Tia, and Triceratops bestie Kai as they tackle kid-shaped problems with dino-sized solutions! Tim, Tommy, Tia and Dad get stuck on a remote asteroid.
Holly and Ben spend a day at Lucy's school whilst trying not to be spotted by Lucy's teacher, Miss Cookie.
Snooty King and Queen Marigold invite themselves round for dinner to King and Queen Thistle's Castle to sample Nanny Plum's cooking. Nanny tries very hard to cook special modern food.
Grumblestunk's new speed camera catches Stan breaking the speed limit on his scooter, but he can't have been! Stan and Gran have to clear his name!
Stan and Gran get the giggles while spotting nature on the Ley, and the lake seems to be giggling back at them! Who is that laughing?
When Mayor Humdinger transforms his robot cat Meow-Meow into a tiger-sized metal-eating menace, the PAW Patrol calls in the Cat Pack for help in the stopping the creature.

After stowing away on the Turbots' camping trip, Wally the walrus gets stuck in a mountain crevasse, and it's up to Everest and the Paw Patrol to rescue him; Mayor Humdinger challenges Rubble for the right to deejay a dance party.
Baron Bite makes things disappear. The twins sink on a jelly planet!

Mix and Motor's favourite TV star has a new movie playing in Builder Cove. The pups need to build a movie theatre to watch it! Grandpa tells the pups about a buried treasure, they find out the key to finding this treasure is construction teamwork!

When the Duke and Claw use a magic cauldron to put the people of Barkingburg to sleep, their plan backfires when the enchanted fog works on Sparks. It's up to the PAW Patrol to wake up the Dragon along with everyone else in town.

Mayor Humdinger turns up the power on his robotic football cleats, the "Hum-Kickers", and starts wrecking the town. Francois causes musical mayhem, as a one-man band, when he plans a special song for Wally's birthday.
Baron Bite seizes a remote control that Kai was using to help penguins fly. Sir Steel and Blip cause mayhem at the Fix-It-Fair by attempting to fix items that are not broken.
Tim attempts to distract Tia whilst Tusky is being washed in the machine.
Tim, Tommy and Tia find a lost mammoth in their house.
Tim tries to relax, but Tia has other ideas.
CatRat takes Gabby and Pandy on a puzzle hunt through the dollhouse, where they solve riddles, play games and find fun surprised along the way.
Cupcake expert Cakey helps Gabby and Pandy shrink down a giant cupcake tree to rescue CatRat and the Gabby Cats from its overgrown branches.
Papa Smurf wants to prove to Willow that alchemy is more powerful than her natural magic; Brainy's new brain-weighing invention backfires and leaves him brainless.
Rubble & Crew want to help open a new restaurant for everyone at the Buddy Walk Race... but they can't decide what kind of restaurant to build!
The pups must come to the rescue when a family of monkeys scatters into the jungle after being scared off by lava erupting from a volcano.
Ryder and the pups are on their way to the jungle to help Carlos move a relic to the museum, but Carlos falls into a pit. Carlos is then saved by a big-eared pup named Tracker.
The Sea Patrol must save the day when a baby octopus gets separated from its mother and sinks the Flounder.
Madame Gazelle sets the children a creative task of making masks. There are carrot masks, robot masks, and even pretty butterfly masks. The only thing missing is lots and lots of glitter.

Peppa takes Goldie the Goldfish for a visit to the vets and is surprised when she finds that there's a new road to be built over the building! With the help of Mr. Bull and his brother they find that instead of demolishing the vets they can build a tunnel underneath it.
On a beautiful sunny day, Grandpa takes Peppa and George to spend the day sailing. After an accident, the boat ends up sinking, and now they need rescuing with a hovercraft.

Daddy Pig takes Peppa and George to school on their scooters. When he decides that it would be quicker to ride back, he discovers that riding scooters is great fun. Mummy Pig thinks that they are fun too and they both ride the scooters.
While drawing pictures at playgroup, Peppa and her friends learn about each other's families, from Suzy sheep who lives with Mummy Sheep to Freddy Fox who lives with Mr. Fox.
Grandpa Pig and Grandad Dog are on their boats when Grandpa Pig drops an anchor on his foot! After an x-ray and plaster cast at the hospital, Grandpa Pig needs to stay overnight.
Peppa and all her friends are having a sleep-over, with different friends in each of the four different flats in the high street. They decide to play hide and seek across all the rooms.
Ben and Holly are excited when they learn that Nanny Plum is a Tooth Fairy at night. They go along with her to pick up a little girl's tooth, but the little girl is not so little.
Ben and Holly want to play with Gaston the ladybird, but he is missing. Nanny Plum uses her magic crystal ball to find him, and discover his daily routine is not what they thought.
Granny Thistle comes to visit and gives Daisy and Poppy a powerful magical wand. The children escape from the castle and go bananas.
The Wise Old Elf fears an alien invasion after a presumed shooting star lands in the Little Kingdom.
Claw finds a way to make Sparks' breath icy; Chase accidentally pulls the legendary Golden Bone of Excalibark from its stone.
Ryan Reynolds reads stories to help the world fall asleep. Tonight Ryan reads stories that make waves.
A new synthesiser arrives for Daddy Pig, and his family collect sounds for it from around the house while he is out at work.

Peppa and George go bird watching with Grandpa Pig. Peppa quacks like a duck, George coos like a pigeon, and they all have great fun filling in Grandpa Pig's book. Grandpa wants to see a cuckoo, and suddenly he hears one calling.
Mr Labrador is here in his new ice cream van. It is his first day selling ice creams. In fact, Mr Labrador loves ice cream, perhaps a little too much.

Peppa and her friends are at playgroup and today Madame Gazelle would like them all to play music. They think they are playing with normal instruments, but today the children must make their own instruments. Madame Gazelle gathers bits and bobs of old packaging and shows them how to make their own. At the end of the day, they put on a special concert for the parents.

Peppa and her family oversee the building of a large remodel to their home to accommodate the new baby, but things go awry when Daddy Pig's blueprints get swapped for George's plans for a robot house.
Madame Gazelle is giving the playgroup a singing lesson. When the parents arrive, the children perform their song. Madame Gazelle reveals that tomorrow there will be a singing competition.
Mr Elf has built a new boat to replace the one Big Bad Barry ate. He is nervous when the king commands him to take them on a cruise to a tropical paradise.
Ben and Holly meet a new friend, Betty Caterpillar, but she is sad that she can't join in their games because she can't fly.
It's Christmastime in Sodor and every engine is excitedly preparing for the holiday, especially Bruno who is excited to put his star on the tree.
With the holidays just around the corner, Thomas and Percy are determined to deliver the mail to all the patrons of Sodor.
Dora and Diego come to the aid of a baby jaguar lost in the rainforest. Dora, Boots and Diego help a baby owl find its parents and get home.
Tim searches the kitchen, reads labels and ingredients to find a hogweed-free snack for Kai.
Tim tries to find a new rocket that's perfect for him.
Tim and Kai try to give Parky the best day ever.
After seeing an advert for the London Marathon, Daddy Pig applies to take part to show the kids what grit and determination really looks like!
After finding out Daddy Pig has a place in the London Marathon, Peppa and George help Daddy Pig become stronger with lots of different, though not all typical, exercises.
It's the day of the London Marathon! Peppa and family come to cheer Daddy on. Peppa and George see many runners dressed in funny costumes - and then they spot Daddy!
Peppa and George play at Granny and Grandpa Pig's house. Grandma, Peppa and George go to the shed to see what Grandpa is doing and discover that he's built a robot.
Peppa and her friends learn how to animate their drawings at playgroup.
Mum, Dad, Peppa and George decide to go to the beach on a beautiful sunny day. Suddenly, a little cloud covers the sun for a minute, but then it passes and the sun reappears.
Grandpa Pig is taking Peppa and George for a day on his boat. They meet Mr Bull who is using his digger boat to remove all the rubbish in the river that shouldn't be there.
Nanny Plum takes the Fairy children for a nature class in the woods and bumps into the Wise Old Elf who is teaching a nature class to the Elf children.
Queen Thistle reads the children a story, which inspires a question. They can't find the answer in the magic books in the castle, so they go to the Wise Old Elf in the Great Elf Library.
Peppa and George wake up in Granny and Grandpa's motorbike tent by the sea. Peppa finds a message in a bottle with a telephone number on it.
Peppa's Playgroup has a garden outside. The children are all having fun growing different plants and playing hide and seek in the wild wood.
Mr Meerkat shows the children a huge wall that needs painting. They create a fantastic mural using lots of different techniques: brushes, sponges, buggy ropes and even a paint cannon!

Peppa and family are on the search for a new home but after all the house viewings, nothing beats their home. Peppa then suggests they extend their house instead, so the family design a bigger house together.

Peppa and friends are at school where they have a special guest, Mr Potato. Together they sing the vegetable song about the importance of eating five fruits or vegetables a day. Mr Potato is there to host a special quiz about fruit and vegetables. They argue about a tomato being a vegetable and have to call up a very clever friend to help. Two groups of children compete to find out who knows the most.
Miss Rabbit's Rescue Service has saved many people from tricky situations, but what happens when Miss Rabbit needs rescuing herself.
The Pig family go to the hospital, where Peppa is determined to find the perfect name for the baby.

Mummy Pig and Peppa are at the zoo and meet Lorenzo Lion who lives there; he is helping his daddy, Mr. Lion the zookeeper, take care of the zoo; Lorenzo shows Peppa his toy zoo, but he keeps misplacing his wooden animals in his two bedrooms!

Peppa and her family take Goldie the Fish to Doctor Hamster for her check-up. They see Grampy Rabbit and his pet newt. Doctor Hamster tells Grampy Rabbit about how she wishes she could exercise more but doesn't have any room. Grampy Rabbit decides to build something special to help Dr Hamster exercise more.
Peppa, George and Freddy Fox are mistaken for pirates while sailing on the river with Grandpa Pig. When the truth is revealed, officers Panda and Squirrel invite them for a ride in their police boat.
During a picnic in her garden, cousin Chloe shows Peppa and George fun things to do with flowers.
Auntie, Uncle Pig, and cousin Chloe are coming for dinner and Peppa is allowed to join too! Peppa is very proud of staying up late; she even stayed up later than the Daddies!
Mummy Pig and Peppa are at Granny Pig's house. They find Mummy's old patchwork quilt that Granny made for her as a baby. Peppa decides she'd like to make one for the baby!
Peppa eagerly awaits her new sibling, growing impatient with the lengthy wait. Suddenly, Mummy Pig announces that the baby is coming right now.
Madame Gazelle needs to go to the dentist and Bull takes over Peppa's class. As the children already know the suggested themes, Bull decides to show them how to fix a floorboard that is creaking.
Peppa and George go behind the scenes to find out how TV is made when Miss Rabbit shows them around the set of Super Potato's TV show.
Mummy and Daddy Pig show Peppa and George how to play flying discs in the park. Soon their friends appear with their parents.
Peppa celebrates Goldie's birthday by holding an undersea party - by turning the house into an underwater environment.

Mummy Pig, Daddy Pig, Peppa and George go to the skate park with their bicycles, scooters and skateboards. While Peppa has fun playing around on Daddy's skateboard, she soon learns that he is more of an expert than she realised.

Granny and Grandpa Pig have been growing strawberries to make jam, but the birds have eaten all the fruit. They decide to go and pick their own at Miss Rabbit's strawberry farm, but Granny and Grandpa eat too many strawberries and end up very full.
Peppa and her friends visit the Little Cars Play Centre where Miss Rabbit is in charge, and they get to drive little toy cars.
Mr Bull builds a brand-new clubhouse and slide for Peppa and her friends.
It's a snowy day and Peppa's family build an igloo for their snowman. They hide in it during a snowstorm, but Penny Polar Bear and her parents love snowstorms and also Peppa's igloo.
The children learn about the weather, there is a new friend for Peppa, and Peppa and George visit Granny and Grandpa's where Grandpa Pig is making a Rock Garden.
Mandy Mouse has a birthday visit to a cheese theme park with Peppa and her friends. Everything in the park is cheese-themed, and Mandy loves cheese.
Inspired by Granny Pig's stories of ancient Rome, Peppa and George decide to design the mosaic of a dinosaur with pebbles, and learn a little Latin.
While enjoying a tea break, Mr Bull accidentally breaks his delicate teapot. He takes the pieces to Miss Rabbit in the hope that she can mend it.
Peppa is feeling unwell and Doctor Brown Bear says she must stay in bed. Peppa's friends come to cheer her up.
Peppa and family go camping, but soon realise that their tent is too small for everyone, so Daddy sleeps underneath the stars.
Grandpa Pig takes Peppa and George to the playground, but does not understand the children's rules.
Suzy and Peppa start a Secret Club where they go on secret missions, and do secret things, but soon everyone wants to join.
Doctor Hamster is rushed off her feet when nearly all the animals need her help on the same day.
Peppa and George visit Mr Fox's Shop to buy Granny and Grandpa an anniversary present, but have trouble choosing from the shop that sells everything.
Peppa's friends are all riding their bicycles. Peppa is determined to learn to cycle without her stabilisers after she teases George about having a baby's tricycle.
It's raining, and Peppa is sad because she cannot play outside. However, when the rain stops, Peppa and George get to play one of their favourite games, namely jumping in muddy puddles.
When the police visit the school, officers Panda and Squirrel teach Peppa and her friends all about bicycle safety.
Peppa and her family travel to Paris to visit Delphine and her relatives. The donkeys take Peppa and her family to the top of the Eiffel Tower, forcing Dad to face his fear of heights.
Peppa and George are taken to visit the home that Mr Bull is building. They could also find out who their new neighbours are going to be.
Peppa's car runs out of petrol, but Granddad Dog's garage is nearby, and with one call, Granddad Dog is on his way to help.
Peppa and her family follow a nature trail in the countryside, discovering footprints left by little birds and ants.
Peppa learns that Mummy Pig used to keep a diary when she was her age, so Peppa decides to give it a try.
PC Panda brings his twin daughters to playgroup Peggy and Pandora Panda. They love puzzles and to solve mysteries just like their dad.
Peppa and George visit Granny and Grandpa Pig. Grandpa builds a special hiding hut to watch birds in so they can all go owl-spotting.

Peppa and her family are going for a drive. Suddenly their car breaks down, and it has to go to Granddad Dog's garage to be fixed. While their car is fixed, they borrow a shiny new, blue car from Granddad Dog.

Doctor Hamster comes to school to talk about butterflies. Doctor Hamster shows the children some colourful caterpillars and all the children draw pictures of caterpillars. One caterpillar forms a chrysalis that opens to reveal a pretty butterfly. The children paint butterfly wings and dance the life cycle of a butterfly.
Mummy, Daddy, Peppa and George go to the park. Peppa and George play on the hopping logs, the bouncing branch and the monkey bars.
When Daddy Pig is given a parking ticket, Peppa and George learn that adults have rules just like children - and that they get told off too.
When Peppa decides to walk up the big hill during their family hike in the countryside, Daddy Pig assures her that the hard climb will be worth it.
Madame Gazelle is making a wicker basket. She explains it is her hobby - something you do to relax. The children discuss hobbies and learn about each other's favourite things to do.
With the building work complete, it's time to decorate! Peppa and George have fun choosing how to decorate their new attic bedrooms. It's dinosaurs for George, but what will Peppa pick?
Peppa and George are re-enacting the Apollo Moon Landing with the help of Granny Pig's friends. Grampy Rabbit lends them his rocket, but no one has told him it's just pretend.
When George loses the metal wind-up key for his toy robot in the long grass, Grandpa Pig cannot find his metal detector to help George track it down.
Peppa and her friends have fun while painting in the playgroup. Madame Gazelle then teaches them how to play games with parachutes.
It's the day of the London Marathon! Peppa and family come to cheer Daddy on. Peppa and George see many runners dressed in funny costumes - and then they spot Daddy!
Peppa and George check out Grandpa's new Bug Hotel as lots of insects arrive. A bumblebee cannot find a place in the hotel because the rooms are too small for him.

Madame Gazelle presents the poetry to Peppa and her friends, explaining that sounds can also be poems. When it starts raining, the inspired children create a beautiful poem about the rain and recite it to their parents.
Peppa, George, Molly Mole and Freddy Fox play in the garden. Molly digs a tunnel and hits a box of pirate treasure.
At playgroup, Madame Gazelle has invited Mr Potato to lead Peppa and her friends in a wonderfully fun musical Kiddie Workout.
Mr Bull builds a brand-new clubhouse and slide for Peppa and her friends.

Peppa and her family are visiting Cousin Chloe's house to play with Baby Alexander. Peppa thinks she knows all about babies because she already looks after her doll, and George is a baby too, though he disagrees.
Teddy needs mending and cleaning after rolling down hills and jumping in muddy puddles, so Peppa takes her to Miss Rabbit's Doll Hospital.
Granny and Grandpa Pig have a beautiful little boat, and Peppa and George are spending the day on the river with them.

It is school project time for Peppa and her friends, which means they have to build castles and bring them into playgroup. Mummy and Daddy Pig have lots of fun helping Peppa make hers, if only they could find the glitter.
Peppa and her playgroup friends go with Madame Gazelle to visit Pedro Pony, who is poorly in hospital.

It is time for a day out and Peppa, George, Mummy Pig, Daddy Pig and Suzy Sheep all go to visit Tiny Land. They see tiny dinosaurs, their favourite tiny landmarks and even a tiny Miss Rabbit doing even more jobs.
Peppa and George help Mummy Pig tidy up the breakfast things. Mummy Pig teaches them how to recycle the bottles and newspapers, then they take everything to Miss Rabbit at the recycling plant.
Peppa and her family visit a museum, and Peppa likes the Kings and Queens room, whereas George's favourite is the dinosaur room.
Peppa's family is staying at Cousin Chloe's house. It's been a long day and everyone is tired and sleepy, but baby Alexander keeps everyone awake with his crying.
When Grandpa Pig puts up a tent in his garden, Peppa and her friends decide that it's a perfect place to put on a circus. With Peppa as the ringmaster, the show can begin.
Peppa and George are playing in the garden when they hear a strange noise. It's thunder. Peppa and George are a little bit frightened at first but Peppa soon decides that she loves thunderstorms.
Peppa and her family spot a rainbow when they go for a drive.
Peppa and her family are trying to get to the playground, but Mr Bull's roadworks are in the way.

Peppa and George's toy basket is full, and their beds are covered in toys, so Mummy Pig decides it is time to order a new toy cupboard. The cupboard arrives in the post, but it needs to be assembled - and Mummy and Daddy Pig are not very good at DIY. Luckily help is at hand, as Mr Zebra the Postman loves assembling flat-pack furniture.
Granny and Grandpa's pet Polly Parrot comes to stay, and Peppa and George love Polly Parrot. But when she flies away, no one knows what to do.
Grandpa Pig has built a fantastic little train called Gertrude, and when they take a ride, they give all their friends a ride.
When Peppa goes for a sleepover at Zoe Zebra's house with Suzy Sheep, Rebecca Rabbit, Candy Cat and Emily Elephant, the girls are too excited to go to sleep.
It's nighttime at Grandpa and Granny Pig's house, and Peppa and George have stayed up late to help hunt for slugs and snails. But what other night animals will they find?
Peppa and George make everyone laugh when they dress up as Mummy and Daddy Pig.
When Daddy Pig loses his glasses he gets a bit grumpy, but Peppa and George have lots of fun looking for them.
Madame Gazelle takes Peppa and her friends on a train ride where they must tick off what they see on their activity sheets.
Peppa and family go on a walk through the forest where they meet all of their favourite fairytale characters. They visit the home of bears who like porridge and meet a hungry Mr Wolf.
Peppa and all her friends at playgroup dress up as different countries from all over the world.
Peppa and George are playing in Grandpa Pig's garden when they find a little snail.
Peppa and Suzy Sheep are best friends, but one day they have a quarrel over a game of cards and decide they are not best friends any more.
Peppa, George, Granny and Grandpa Pig visit the sailing club where they find a juke box. They have fun dancing to all different types of music.
Peppa and her friends visit Mrs Badger's petting farm, where they enjoy feeding the chickens and meeting cute guinea pigs.
Peppa's family embarks on an adventure, but Daddy Pig's fear of heights threatens their climb to the monkey tree.
Peppa is playing with Candy Cat when Emily Elephant's Granny moves out of the flat. When the new neighbours arrive, Peppa recognises her holiday friend Rohan Rhino.
George undergoes a medical examination to assess his hearing. The results of the test reveal moderate hearing loss in his left ear, marking an important milestone in his health and development.

While visiting Suzy and Emily's house, Peppa is surprised that there are extra rules which she does not have in her own house. On the drive home, Peppa explains to Mummy Pig that different houses have different rules.

Mummy Pig takes Peppa to the doctors for her yearly health check-up with Dr Polar Bear, who checks her height, weight, ears, mouth and heartbeat and listens to Mummy tell him all about the changes Peppa has gone through.
Peppa and her friends visit the cinema for the first time to watch the 'Super Potato' film.
Peppa and George play at Granny and Grandpa's house and have a fun dinosaur party.
Peppa helps out with Danny Dog refurbishing his bedroom, and imagines a pirate adventure along the way.
Grandpa Pig finds his night at the hospital so comfortable, he's reluctant to be discharged. Papa and Suzy volunteer to nurse him at home and make sure he's just as comfortable as he was in hospital.
Peppa and her friends are at their clubhouse. They decide to start a detective club, and when Daddy Pig loses his car keys, they have a real mystery to solve.
While Mummy Pig is enjoying a spa day out, Daddy, George and Peppa explore the rest of the shopping centre.
Mummy Pig shows Peppa how to play pretend by teaching her how to wink. Zoe Zebra comes to play with Peppa and brings along her toy monkey. Peppa pretends Monkey has a cough.
Peppa and her family go bowling at the Peppatown Bowling Alley.
Peppa and her friends visit a roller disco organised by Madame Gazelle. After skating along to nursery rhymes, they go wild to the rhythm of the music together with Madame Gazelle.
Peppa and George join Grandma Piggy and her friends to play a game pretending to be Vikings. The Vikings enjoy Grandpa Piggy's boat until they realise they forgot about the picnic.
When the school roof is broken and needs fixing, Peppa volunteers Mummy Pig to do a parachute jump to raise money. Daddy Pig goes up too, and has to overcome his fear of heights.

Mummy Pig's book is finished, and it's time to show it off to Peppa and her playgroup friends. Unfortunately, Peppa and George lose some of the book when they are playing, and Mummy Pig has to think quickly to fix it.
Peppa and George love going to the beach on sunny days. They bring their water wings, a beach ball and buckets and spades. Peppa and George have fun burying Daddy Pig in the sand.
Peppa and George go on a boat trip with Grandpa Pig, but they must send Polly Parrot for help when their boat runs aground. Polly fetches Granny Pig and Grandad Dog to rescue them.
Peppa and her friends and family are looking forward to a trip to the seaside where they can make sandcastles, but when they arrive at the beach there is too much snow.
Mrs Zebra teaches Peppa, George, Zoe, Zaza and Zuzu Zebra how to make a real tea set from clay.
Madame Gazelle takes the class to London for the day, where they are given a tour of the city by none other than the Queen of England.
Madame Gazelle takes Peppa and her school friends on a school bus trip to the mountains. From the top of the mountains, there is a fantastic view, and Peppa and her friends have fun hearing echoes.
Playgroup is having a pet competition and everyone has brought their pets. Dr Hamster is the judge, but it is so hard to choose the best pet.
Peppa and her friends are playing pirates, but when they put together a treasure chest and bury it in a marked spot, Pedro soon realises that he needs to follow the trail. He's lost something.
Mummy Pig and Daddy Pig are going out for the evening. Granny and Grandpa Pig babysit Peppa and George. They are too excited to sleep. When Mummy Pig and Daddy Pig get home everyone is asleep.
Peppa and Luzie Locke find that adults have to work all the time. The children imitate the elders, in the shop and on the playground. They realise that playing can be really hard work.
Peppa and her friends learn how to count by playing games at Madame Gazelle's playschool.
Madame Gazelle gives the class a music lesson. There's lots of crashing and banging at first, but it's not long before the grown-ups visit and lay down some notes of their own.
George has fun making bubbles, and Peppa has fun popping them.
Suzy Sheep has come to play with Peppa, and has made up a pretend friend called 'Leo Lion'. Peppa can't see Leo, but Suzy announces that Leo likes roaring and playing dressing up.
It's Daddy Pig's birthday, but he has to go to work, so while he's away, Mummy Pig, Peppa and George prepare a special birthday surprise.
Daddy Pig is left behind when everyone takes Grampy Rabbit's little boat to the riverside picnic spot. Will someone remember him and save him some cake?
When Daddy Pig and Mummy Pig are tidying up the house, they happen to find an old box of musical instruments. George makes a loud sound with the Swiss horn.
Peppa and George love helping Mummy Pig work on her computer, but they like playing computer games more.
The youngsters visit the zoo where they are shown around by zookeepers Mr Lion, Mrs Crocodile and Mr Giraffe.
Peppa and George are helping Grandpa Pig to dig a new pond for his garden. While digging, they find hidden treasure so they go to see Mr Richard in the museum.
Dr Hamster's pet tortoise, Tiddles, once again gets stuck on top of a tree, but everyone in the rescue team finds it tough to get the tortoise down.
Peppa and her family are at the swimming pool. George is a little worried at first but is soon splashing happily with his friend Richard Rabbit.
Peppa and George are helping Granny and Grandpa Pig tidy their attic, but they have trouble deciding what to throw out because Granny and Grandpa want to keep everything.

It's a beautiful day but Peppa, George and Grandpa Pig are sitting inside watching the motor racing on the television. Granny Pig shoos them all outside to enjoy the sunshine. Inspired by the racing, Grandpa Pig builds George his own racing car.
Peppa and George visit Granny Pig, who is very excited about her new pet, a parrot called Polly.
Peppa and George have to tidy their bedroom. After a frenzy of cleaning, the room is tidy, but the room doesn't stay tidy for long though.
Daddy Pig hangs his clean football shirt out to dry, but Peppa, George and Mummy splash it with mud. They put it in the wash, but Peppa puts her red dress in too, which turns Daddy's shirt pink.
Doctor Hamster visits the school and brings some animals with her. Binky the Tortoise is very popular, but ends up needing to be rescued by Miss Rabbit.
Peppa and her family collect apples and blackberries in Granny and Grandpa Pig's garden to make a pie.
Madame Gazelle gets Peppa and her playgroup friends to dance to all different styles of music.
The grass has grown so long that Peppa and George's ball gets lost in it. It falls to Grandpa to save the day with Betsy, his motorised lawnmower.
George pays a visit to Mr Fox's Shop after his favourite toy, Mr Dinosaur, breaks. With all the additional features, surely Dino Roar is a good replacement?
It's fruit day at the market and Miss Rabbit is making smoothies from people's favourite fruit. She gives George a special 'dinosaur' juice to make him big and strong.
Peppa and George have fun in the snow, as they make footprints, snowballs and build a snowman.
Mummy Pig has a lovely new picture of Peppa and George, so Daddy Pig offers to put it up, but it's not as simple as Daddy Pig thought, and he makes a very big hole in the wall.
Goldie the fish does not look happy and is not eating her food. Peppa, George, and Mummy Pig take her on a bus trip to visit Dr Hamster the vet.

Peppa has a new pen pal, a little donkey from France named Delphine. Peppa receives letters from Delphine Donkey and speaks to her on the telephone. Although Peppa speaks English and Delphine speaks French, they discover that they love lots of the same things, especially jumping up and down in muddy puddles.
Granny Pig is really pleased with all the plastic gnomes and wishing well she's got for the garden. Peppa and George love them too, but Grandpa Pig wishes they would all disappear.

Mummy and Daddy Pig let Peppa and George put their coats on over their pyjamas and go outside to look at the stars. With the help of a telescope, Daddy Pig teaches Peppa and George how to find the North Star.

When a fishing trip goes wrong, leaving Grandpa Pig and Grampy Rabbit stranded on a desert island, Captain Daddy Dog is the only one able to save them. It makes him realise that he misses the sea after all.
Peppa loves secrets, so Mummy Pig makes her a special box to put secret things in.

Peppa's best friend, Suzy Sheep, comes to play at Peppa's house for the afternoon. Peppa won't allow George to join in. When Peppa and Suzy want to play doctors and nurses, George is delighted to be the patient.
Granny and Grandpa Pig come for a dinner party with Mummy and Daddy Pig. Peppa and George are too tired to go to bed until they are told a story.
Daddy Pig winds up the old cuckoo clock in Peppa and George's bedroom. When the clock strikes the hour, a wooden bird pops out, flapping its wings and singing 'Cuckoo'.
Daddy teaches the children how to play basketball, and it is not long before they are good enough to take on a much bigger team.

Bei einem Eignungstest stell sich heraus, dass Arnold eine Intelligenzbestie und Helga eher für ein Landleben geeignet ist. Oskar hat Schulden und muss arbeiten, um das Geld zurückzahlen zu können. Er lässt aber Arnold an seiner Stelle arbeiten.

Curly ist an der Reihe, die Bälle einsammeln und wegräumen zu dürfen, doch Sid nimmt ihm die Aufgabe weg. Daraufhin dreht Curly durch. Phoebe gewinnt einen Abend mit Rockstar Ronnie und ist enttäuscht, als sie ihr Idol singen hört.

Stinky wird für einen Hollywood-Werbespot ausgesucht. Seine Freude hält nicht lange an. Er erfährt, dass er nur gewählt wurde, weil er als dämlich eingeschätzt wurde. Olga will heiraten, woraufhin Helga hofft, ihre Schwester endlich los zu sein.

Arnold besucht seine Lieblingsautorin Agatha Caulfield, um über sie zu schreiben. Doch sie will ihm partout kein Interview geben. Der neue Schüler Lorenzo kommt an die Schule. Er ist reich und benimmt sich wie ein Erwachsener.

Helga wurde beim Zahnarzt betäubt und gesteht Arnold auf dem Anrufbeantworter, dass sie ihn liebt. Harold hat in der Metzgerei einen Schinken gestohlen und muss dort nun eine Woche lang ohne Lohn arbeiten. Er freundet sich mit seinem Chef an.

Arnold sieht, wie Iggy krank in einem Kleinkinderschlafanzug im Bett liegt. Er findet das so lustig, dass er den anderen Kindern davon erzählt. Das neue Kindermädchen Inge soll auf Helga aufpassen. Sie und Helga verstehen sich aber überhaupt nicht.

Arnold verletzt beim Baseballspiel immer andere Kinder und traut sich nicht mehr, zu spielen. Beim Endspiel überwindet er sich aber und gewinnt. Mr. Hyunh nimmt eine CD mit Countrysongs auf. Als die Musik im Radio spielt, wird er berühmt.

Sid und Lorenzo sind am Nachmittag verabredet, weil sie gemeinsam eine Arbeit machen müssen. Weil Lorenzo eine schönere Wohnung hat, will sich Sid lieber bei ihm treffen. Außerdem hat Helga Angst vor Patty, weil sie über sie gelästert hat.

Die Kinder schauen sich im Berufsleben um. Arnold geht zum Jolly Olly Man, der Kinder hasst. Arnold muss die ganze Zeit sauber machen. Harold kann Mädchen nicht ausstehen und geht zu einer Party. Als er Patty trifft, freundet er sich mit ihr an.

Das Haus von Thaddäus wird von einem Flohzirkus heimgesucht, der für SpongeBob bestimmt ist. Zudem täuscht Thaddäus vor, krank zu sein, um nicht arbeiten zu müssen, aber seine Qualen beginnen erst, als SpongeBob kommt, um ihn zu pflegen.

Weil Patrick sich als Wurm ausgibt, kommt er ins Tierheim und kann nur raus, wenn SpongeBob ihn richtig erziehen kann. Nachdem die Band vom 1000-Taubenüsschen-Nusseis-Partyboot gefeuert wird, versuchen SpongeBob und Patrick sie wieder zu vereinen.

Als es einem Baum in Sandys Zuhause schlecht geht, bittet sie Thaddäus, den Baum zu heilen, doch seine ungewöhnlichen Methoden sorgen für Probleme. SpongeBob und Thaddäus suchen das perfekte Geburtstagsgeschenk für Mr. Krabs.

SpongeBob und Patrick erfahren, dass ihre Superhelden in einem nahegelegenen Altersheim wohnen. Als die beiden "Meerjungfraumann" und "Blaubarsch-Bube" besuchen, wollen sie ihre Helden aus der Vergangenheit zu einem Comeback überreden.
Die Freundinnen erhöhen nach Sandys Karatekurs ihre Leistung. Bald macht die ganze Stadt mit. Plankton kommt heimlich auf Karens Party, doch sie durchschaut ihn sofort.

SpongeBob bewirbt sich in der Krossen Krabbe, außerdem reinigen SpongeBob und Thaddäus ihre Vorgärten, und SpongeBob ist bei Sandy zum Tee eingeladen. Allerdings gibt es in der Glaskuppel, in der sie wohnt, kein Wasser.

SpongeBob eröffnet vor seinem Haus einen Stand zum Seifenblasen pusten und da Patrick am Anfang Schwierigkeiten beim Seifenblasen-Pusten hat, bietet er auch einen Anfängerkurs an, außerdem reißt SpongeBob bei einem Date mit Sandy die Hose.

Patrick und SpongeBob lieben das Quallenfischen, obwohl sie dabei stets erfolglos sind, nun wollen sei auch Thaddäus an dieses Hobby heranführen. Plankton hat es wieder auf die Geheimformel abgesehen und nistet sich dafür in SpongeBobs Hirn ein.
